sera: sērus, -a, -um — late, tardy (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.) · also f. abl. sg. (sera nocte)
simul: simul (adv.) — at the same time, together
sinistra: sinister, -tra, -trum — left, on the left (f. abl. sg., sc. manū; also f. nom. sg.)
siqua: sī + qua — if any, if in any way (indef. qua, f. nom. sg., with gloria) · also n. acc. pl. (siqua dona, any gifts)
siquid: sī quis — if any(thing) (indef.; siquid = sī quid, n. nom./acc. sg.; siquid veri, 'if aught of truth')
solabar: sōlor, sōlārī, sōlātus sum — to console, comfort (1st sg. impf., deponent)
spargebat: spargō, -ere, sparsī, sparsum — to scatter, strew, sprinkle (3rd sg. impf.)
spissa: spissus, -a, -um — thick, dense, packed (f. abl. sg.)
spolia: spolium, -ī (n.) — spoils, armour stripped from a foe (acc./nom. pl.)
spoliisque: spolium, -ī (n.) — spoil, booty, plunder (abl./dat. pl.) + -que, and
stant: stō, stāre, stetī, statum — to stand, stand firm (3rd pl. pres.)
sub: sub (prep.) — + abl. under, beneath; + acc. up to, under
subitus: subitus, -a, -um — sudden, unexpected (adj., m. nom. sg.)
sum: sum, esse, fuī — to be (1st sg. pres.)
suscitat: suscitō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to rouse, stir up, raise (3rd sg. pres.)
tabo: tābum, -ī (n.) — gore, corrupted blood, ooze (abl. sg.)
tam: tam (adv.) — so, so much, to such a degree
tanta: tantus, -a, -um — so great, such (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.) · also f. abl. sg. (ex tantā urbe)
tartara: Tartarus, -ī (m.); pl. Tartara, -ōrum (n.) — the underworld, the nether depths (acc./nom. pl.)
tela: tēlum, -ī (n.) — missile, weapon, spear, dart (acc./nom. pl.)
telorum: tēlum, -ī (n.) — missile, weapon, spear, dart (gen. pl.)
tenent: teneō, tenēre, tenuī, tentum — to hold, keep, restrain (3rd pl. pres.)
terra: terra, -ae (f.) — land, earth, ground (nom./abl. sg.) · also f. voc. sg. (ō terra hospita)
testudine: testūdō, -inis (f.) — tortoise; vaulted roof, arch (abl. sg.)
teucri: Teucer, Teucrī (m.) — Teucer, early king of Troy (gen. sg.) · also Teucrī, -ōrum (m. pl.) Trojans (voc. pl.: Teucrī, secludite) · also m. nom. pl. (Teucrī, Trojans)
tibi: tū, tuī — you (sg.); tibi, to/for you (dat.)
tithoni: Tithōnus, -ī (m.) — Tithonus, Trojan prince, husband of Aurora (gen. sg.)
tua: tuus, -a, -um — your, yours (sg. poss.) (f. nom. sg.) · also n. acc. pl. (tua nūmina) · also f. abl. sg. (tua laude)
tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
tune: tū, tuī — you (sg.) + -ne (interrog. enclitic): tūne, is it you…?
turnus: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, young king of the Rutulians, suitor of Lavinia (nom. sg.)
una: ūnus, -a, -um — one, a single (f. abl./nom. sg.); ūnā (adv.), together · also ūnā, adv., once (satis ūnā superque, enough once and more)
vallo: vallum, -ī (n.) — rampart, palisaded wall (abl. sg.; also dat. sg.)
variisque: varius, -a, -um — various, manifold, different (f. abl. pl., with arboribus) + -que 'and' · also n. abl. pl.
vellere: vellō, -ere, vellī (vulsī), vulsum — to pluck, tear up (pres. inf.)
vires: vīs (f.) — force; pl. vīrēs, strength (acc. pl.) · also nom. pl. (fractae vīrēs)
virum: vir, virī (m.) — man, hero (acc. sg.; also gen. pl., old form = virōrum)
visu: vīsus, -ūs (m.) — sight, seeing (abl. sg.; miserābile vīsū, pitiable to see)
volcentem: Volcens (Volscens), -entis (m.) — Volcens, Latin captain of horse (acc. sg.)
volitans: volitō, -āre — to flit, fly about (pres. part., f. nom. sg., with Fama) · also m. nom. sg.
vos: tū, vōs — you (2nd pers. pl. pron.) (nom./acc. pl.) · also voc. pl. (vōs, aetērnī ignēs)
